project-charter.title: Observe Springs in Real Applications

cards.title: Client Brief & Study Scope
cards.body: Tata Motors & Bajaj Auto Central R&D Division requires you to perform a comparative engineering evaluation of four fundamental spring arrangements used in mechanical systems: Helical Compression, Helical Tension, Concentric Helical Compression, and Multi-Leaf Springs.

cards.title: Four Mechanical Applications Under Study
cards.body:
1. Motorcycle Rear Suspension (Helical Compression Spring)
2. Mechanical Return Mechanism (Helical Tension / Extension Spring)
3. Engine Valve Mechanism (Concentric Helical Compression Springs)
4. Commercial Vehicle Rear Axle (Multi-Leaf Spring)

cards.title: Engineering Objectives
items: Identify the four spring configurations on Engineering Asset EA-14.
Match spring types with primary loading modes and operational functions.
Compare constructional geometry, space constraints, and performance trade-offs.
Evaluate engineering scenarios to select the optimal spring configuration.
Formulate a comparative engineering recommendation report.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have read and understood the EA-14 Project Charter for Spring Comparative Study & Selection.

component-identification.title: Identify the Four Spring Configurations
component-identification.description: Student engineering asset illustrating four real-world spring applications and configurations.

labels.feedback: Single coiled spring operating under axial push/compression.
Close-wound spring with end hooks operating under pull/tension.
Dual co-axial compression springs nested inside each other.
Laminated steel leaves clamped together operating under bending.
Upper frame eyelet supporting motorcycle rear shock unit.
Fixed pin anchoring extension spring loop.
High-speed valve stem with split collets holding dual spring seats.
Heavy-duty U-bolts clamping leaf spring stack to rear axle housing.

application-function-match.title: Identify Application and Function
application-function-match.prompt: Analyze the functional role of each spring type in its respective engineering application.

mcq.question: Which option correctly pairs the spring type with its primary functional purpose?

options.label: Concentric Springs → Engine Valve → High spring force in compact space & valve bounce prevention
Extension Spring → Commercial Vehicle Axle → Heavy vertical load carrying
Leaf Spring → Actuating Mechanism → High speed pull return force
Helical Compression Spring → Engine Valve → Pure tension pulling

loading-conditions-compare.title: Compare Loading Conditions
loading-conditions-compare.prompt: Evaluate the primary mechanical stress and load state acting on the spring material.

mcq.question: Which statement accurately describes the primary internal stress state induced in the wire/leaf material?

options.label: Helical compression & extension springs experience torsional shear stress in the wire; leaf springs experience transverse bending stress across the leaves.
Helical compression springs experience pure tensile stress while leaf springs experience pure shear stress.
All four spring types experience identical direct compressive stress without any torsion or bending.
Extension springs experience radial crushing stress while concentric springs experience hydrostatic pressure.

construction-geometry-compare.title: Compare Construction and Geometry
construction-geometry-compare.prompt: Examine the geometric arrangement and construction features of concentric compression springs vs single compression springs.

mcq.question: Why are concentric springs wound with opposite helix hand directions (one right-hand, one left-hand)?

options.label: To prevent the coils of the inner and outer springs from interlocking or binding during axial deflection.
To make the inner spring rotate in the opposite direction of engine crankshaft.
To balance the magnetic field generated by high-speed spring motion.
To reduce the cost of spring steel material by 50%.

design-requirements-compare.title: Compare Design Requirements
design-requirements-compare.prompt: Compare the operating environment and packaging constraints across the four applications.

mcq.question: Which application imposes the strictest constraint regarding high cyclic operating frequency and resonance (surge) avoidance?

options.label: Engine valve springs operating at up to 6000 RPM requiring high natural frequency to prevent surge and valve float.
Commercial vehicle leaf springs operating at 1 cycle per hour.
Motorcycle sidestand return spring operating twice per trip.
Parking brake extension spring operating once per parking event.

performance-advantages-compare.title: Compare Performance, Advantages and Limitations
performance-advantages-compare.prompt: Evaluate the engineering trade-offs regarding energy storage, load capacity, and fail-safe reliability.

mcq.question: What is a major advantage of using concentric helical compression springs in IC engine valve trains?

options.label: Fail-safe redundancy: if one spring breaks, the remaining spring prevents the valve from dropping into the cylinder cavity.
Zero manufacturing cost and elimination of heat treatment requirements.
Ability to operate without any lubrication or spring seats.
Elimination of all torsional shear stresses in both springs.

components.name: Heavy Mining Dump Truck Rear Axle
components.label: Suspension Payload & Damping Trade-Off

options.title: SELECT CONCENTRIC SPRINGS FOR VALVE TRAIN & LEAF SPRINGS FOR TRUCK
options.description: Concentric springs provide high force density and fail-safe safety in tight engine head envelopes; leaf springs provide high load capacity and structural axle location for heavy trucks.

options.title: SELECT SINGLE HELICAL COMPRESSION SPRING FOR BOTH APPLICATIONS
options.description: Single compression spring would coil bind or surge in engine head, and lack lateral load guidance and heavy capacity required for truck rear axle.

components.name: Commuter Motorcycle Twin Shock Rear Suspension
components.label: Motorcycle Rear Suspension Selection

options.title: TENSION SPRING FOR THROTTLE RETURN & COMPRESSION SPRING FOR MOTORCYCLE
options.description: Helical tension spring pulls throttle linkage back to idle position safely; helical compression spring provides smooth ride comfort and progressive energy absorption under passenger load.

options.title: LEAF SPRING FOR THROTTLE RETURN & CONCENTRIC SPRINGS FOR MOTORCYCLE
options.description: Leaf spring is excessively heavy and rigid for throttle pedal; concentric springs add unnecessary cost and complexity to commuter motorcycle rear shocks.

questions.label: 1. Spring Classification & Functional Summary
questions.placeholder: Summarize the 4 spring configurations, their primary loading modes (compression, tension, bending), and key applications.

questions.label: 2. Comparative Selection Matrix & Justification
questions.placeholder: Explain how space constraints, load capacity, dynamic frequency, and fail-safe requirements dictate the engineering spring selection.

questions.label: 3. Maintenance & Failure Mode Considerations
questions.placeholder: Provide comparative maintenance insights for end hook stress concentration (tension springs), surge (valve springs), and inter-leaf fretting (leaf springs).
